coaching.headline: Outkilled and out-sieged, eight structures to one. They played the map while we kept giving up the first body.
coaching.team: Every enemy Fangtooth fell with one of us already dead, which is a shit way to contest a pit. The ending ran the same way: Orb Prime and an inner tower fell right after Scarlett and Feng Mao died, both inhibitors fell with Scarlett down, and the Core followed a fight we lost 1-4. Their Genesis Core went uncontested with all five of us alive.
coaching.lossReflection: The better plan was to play the Fangtooth clock instead of the skirmishes around it. Resetting together before each spawn, with Feng Mao in front and Phase linked to Belica behind him, out of Riktor's first pull, gives either a full-strength contest or a clean cross-map trade for a tower. It does not guarantee the fight, but it stops conceding stacks while players are on the respawn timer.

focus.title: Turn won fights into structures
focus.evidence: Our two other wins came in the same window as our own outer towers falling and took nothing back; only the Primal Fangtooth win produced a prize, and objective damage ended 12,466 against 55,663.
focus.action: After any won fight or neutral objective, the living players hit the nearest enemy tower only when a friendly wave is there to tank it, and take a camp or reset otherwise. The next-game check is a structure taken within ninety seconds of each won fight.

perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim's Belica was the one player who turned up armed. Top hero damage on our side, farm well above her usual pace, and kills in two of our three won fights, including the Yurei kill right before our Primal Fangtooth. That is the standard. Two of her three deaths came after two or more of us were already down in that fight, so once two allies drop, Belica backs off toward tower instead of trading into Ikra or Grux.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: A rough Murdock, no argument. Damage per minute ran about a quarter under Goldilocks324’s own norm, deaths ran over it, and Sparrow took three of his five deaths, including the opening kill of the last fight. On a night like that Murdock plays back behind Feng Mao: when Sparrow is unseen before a fight or objective, he lays Static Traps on her approach, Sting Operation giving him spares, and only steps up once she has shown.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Being the team healer and its crash test dummy is one job too many. Phase died first in three separate fights, to Riktor, Sparrow and Ikra in turn. The link belongs on the team’s damage dealer, and this game that was Belica, so before any objective Phase links her and stays behind her until the enemy shows its opener, Riplash included. Mr_Meat31 still handled the healer half: solid healing and a hand in just under half our kills.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's Scarlett was a bloody mess: hero damage under a third of her usual, dead before two of their three Fangtooths. When Fangtooth is under a minute out and any of us is dead, Scarlett calls the pit off and takes a camp, or a tower elsewhere when a friendly wave is there to tank it. She still led our objective damage and took the Riktor kill in the same window as our Primal Fangtooth.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs opened like a menace, taking first blood off Grux and killing him again early. Then the output went quiet: two takedowns out of our fifteen kills and no objective damage, while Grux finished with the most hero damage in the match. He died less than his usual; keep that. Once Grux and Riktor have both spent their pull, Feng Mao dashes onto Sparrow and saves Earth Shatter for her execute; until then he holds the front.

matchup: Riktor's pull, silence and suppress catch whoever stands closest.
Grux and Yurei are the divers that reach an immobile backline; four of five enemies dealt physical damage.
build: The path leans on abilities and crit in place of the Lightning Hawk and Imperator core.
Tainted Rounds had targets: Grux and Ikra finished with Terminus, and Yurei topped the match in healing.
eternal: Vermis and Serration suit finishing Sparrow.
Melting Point only earns its slot if the enemy builds real armor.
Breach on the ultimate is the conditional alternative, giving up that bonus against tanks.
augment: Keep it: more traps on Grux and Yurei's approach is the peel Murdock supplies himself.
crest: Keep Pacifier, holding the dash as the exit from Riktor's pull rather than the chase.
improvement: Keep Necrosis, Vanquisher and Tainted Rounds.
If Sparrow and the divers keep reaching him, a defensive slot over Nuclear Rounds trades ability damage for survival.
This match does not prove which death that item would have prevented.

matchup: Riktor is a catch support with pull, silence and suppress, and led the match in damage mitigated.
The enemy drafted no healers, so Phase's ally healing was a tool they lacked.
build: Prophecy and Orion push Phase toward basic-attack damage.
Tainted Scepter was our only magical anti-heal, into Terminus on Grux and Ikra and Yurei's healing.
Enra's Blessing was skipped, though its shield on an immobilized ally is the exact Riktor case.
eternal: Lotus with Flawless heals Phase and nearby allies on ability hits.
Prima Donna adds 10% damage to heroes but takes 6% more from all sources.
Immaculate is the conditional alternative for a support who died first in three fights, trading away the damage bonus.
augment: Keep it: Psychic Support refills the linked damage dealer's mana, paying most on Belica's Runic Focus.
crest: Keep Tranquility: its group heal is the right answer to fights Riktor opens.
improvement: Conditional swap: if Riktor keeps landing the first catch, replace Orion with Enra's Blessing, trading basic-attack damage for a shield.
Keep Tainted Scepter for the anti-heal.

matchup: Yurei, a dive bruiser chaining resets onto marked targets, killed Scarlett twice.
Sparrow was the soft gank target; Riktor died seven times, so he can be caught, not burst.
build: Tainted Trident had a target in Yurei's match-high healing.
None of the three adds armor.
eternal: Demiurge, Tri-Core and Memory Leak boost item stats, on-hit damage and mana growth.
Bloatware is the conditional alternative if survival is the problem, trading mana and speed growth for damage reduction.
augment: Coup De Grâce pays only when the marked target dies fast.
Keep it when the team commits behind her.
crest: Keep Nex: its dash rewards being in an ongoing fight.
improvement: Supported conditional swap: an armor item in place of Malady, trading low-health damage and the kill explosion for survival.
Zero armor and six deaths support it; the match does not prove which death it would have prevented.

matchup: Ikra, Sparrow and Grux each killed her once; the physical damage dealers were the threats that reached her.
build: On the core; Noxia bursts a hero hit by two different abilities, once every 8 seconds.
eternal: Keep Aion, Bottomless Vial and Runic Focus.
Philosopher is the alternative for steady gold if river buffs are contested.
augment: Keep Combat Veteran: the movement speed is useful on an immobile mage.
crest: Keep Soulbearer: its shield, lifesteal and speed directly answer Ikra or Grux reaching her.
improvement: Keep it: she sat on the full core and led our damage.
If Ikra, Sparrow and Grux keep reaching her, a defensive slot ahead of Oblivion Crown trades late damage for survival.
This match does not test that.

matchup: Grux is an engage bruiser with a pull, dragging charge, stun ultimate and Terminus lifesteal, and led hero damage.
build: No armor and no The Perforator, which ignores a share of physical armor.
eternal: Roses had little to feed on with two takedowns.
The Maw is the conditional alternative, adding true damage on low-health targets at the cost of takedown gold.
augment: Keep Ichorous Glaive: it suits a diver who finishes targets like Sparrow.
crest: Keep Ortus: it is the tool for reaching Sparrow.
improvement: Supported swap: an armor item in place of Manta Scythe once its farming job is done.
Grux topped the match in hero damage and killed Feng twice.
It gives up minion and isolated-target damage; the match does not prove it saves a specific death.

threats: Chain-CC risk (4 hard-CC abilities, ~3.0s of lockdown): Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s), Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Enemy is 4/5 physical — a single armor item blunts most of their damage; itemize armor on anyone diveable.
Dive threat on our backline: Yurei. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

sparrow.loadout: Weald (Forage + Wind-Rider), augment Endless Hunt, crest Liberator
fedBy: Endless Hunt (augment): Takedowns reset Sparrow's Basic Ability Cooldowns and permanently grant 1 Physical Penetration.
lines: Lead story: Hard to kill. Died 2 times in 29 minutes, fewer deaths than about 87% of Sparrow carry players this patch. The build added healing off damage.
12 takedowns (10 kills, 2 assists) fed: Endless Hunt (augment).
Sparrow dealt 23,585 hero damage, 26% of their team's, with +157 physical power from items.

Penetration: Vanquisher 12; against Murdock (level 16: about 103 physical armor, 91 after penetration; took 12,897 physical damage from heroes, 74% of all hero damage they took) and Phase (level 15: about 122 physical armor, 110 after penetration; took 12,800 physical damage from heroes, 78% of all hero damage they took) that is about 6% and 6% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Imperator (item): Critical Strikes deal 30% more damage.
Weald (Eternal): Damaging an Enemy Hero below 30% Health fires 4 (+1 per 30% Bonus Attack Speed) projectiles that each deal 7 (+1 per level) True Damage.
Sustain: 7% lifesteal; Liberator: Cleanse all Debuffs. Gain a 80 (+100%) Shield for 2.5s.; 2,647 healing recorded.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 2 effects on one trigger: Dust Devil, Weald.
Stack (Finishing damage on low-health targets): 2 effects on one trigger: Vanquisher, Weald. Once a fight started going their way, these finished it.
The Eternal was part of it: Weald (Forage + Wind-Rider) sits on the same triggers as the items (every basic attack set off; finishing damage on low-health targets), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 1 of the 4 players Sparrow killed built physical armor (Phase). Anti-heal on Murdock, Phase, Scarlett, Feng Mao. We killed Sparrow 2 times.

Copy it? Weald (Forage + Wind-Rider): 52.2% in 2,694 Sparrow carry games, above the hero's 50.3%; this 3-item core: 53.3% in 225 games, below the 55.6% of that hero-role's cores. Mixed: copy the part that wins, not the whole setup.
